speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVA was established in 2000 to address the increasingly challenging task of maintaining Singapore's high standards of food safety as well as animal and plant health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Minister Masagos Zulkifli earlier spoke about AVA's efforts in ensuring our food safety and food security.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVA has also steadfastly done its job to safeguard our animal and plant health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In particular, AVA has done well to keep Singapore and Singaporeans well-protected against zoonotic diseases, such as the highly pathogenic avian influenza, or bird flu, and rabies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Over the years, there has been more interest in animal welfare issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Many Singaporeans are showing greater empathy and compassion towards stray animals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The number of pet owners is growing, and many see pets as family members.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: At the same time, there are those who are afraid of animals, while others may consider them as a threat or nuisance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: So, there have been instances where residents want to remove wildlife they deem dangerous or causing a nuisance, but animal welfare groups and animal lovers may have a different view.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In this regard, AVA has worked with animal welfare groups (AWGs), other Government agencies, industry partners and residents to address issues arising from our co-existence with animals in a dense urban setting, while bearing in mind animal welfare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, AVA has worked with AWGs and veterinarians to develop the nationwide Trap-Neuter-Release-Manage (TNRM) programme where stray dogs are sterilised to humanely manage their population and rehoming them where possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We want to ensure that we continue to co-exist harmoniously with wildlife and other animals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks has done well over the years to make Singapore a biophilic city in a garden.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: It has built up deep expertise in terms of our flora and fauna, as well as strong relationships with a wide range of stakeholder groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The transfer will bring about several benefits for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: First, NParks will provide a one-stop service on animal management and animal welfare issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Accordingly, AVS will take on AVA's current role as the first responder for animal-related feedback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: AVS will also deepen existing partnerships with veterinarians and animal-related industries to enhance animal health and welfare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Second, we will be better positioned to manage human-animal issues, as they become increasingly complex.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks will have a comprehensive overview of urban and natural ecologies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Combining NParks’ expertise in wildlife conservation and horticultural science, and AVA’s in animal and plant health, and animal management, this will ensure that efforts to conserve Singapore’s natural heritage are holistic and science-based.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks currently works closely with its 45,000 volunteers in its greening efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: With the transfer, stakeholders who have an interest in animal issues, such as pet owners, community animal caregivers and AWGs, will now become a part of the NPark family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: They will be able to work with NParks’ existing stakeholders to come up with new and innovative solutions for animal issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Third, we can improve our detection of, and response to, zoonotic diseases, and put in place better safeguards for public health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks will now oversee disease detection at all potential points of incursion, for instance at the point of import, from migratory wildlife, and between wildlife and urban animals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Disease response can also be enhanced with the consolidation of NParks’ existing expertise in ecology and animal population studies, with AVA’s expertise in veterinary science and diagnostic testing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 3 sets out NParks’ new functions, which include: the protection of animal welfare and animal and plant health, the management of animal population, the prevention of threats and risks arising from animals and plants, to public health and safety, the regulation of trade in endangered animals and plants, and the regulation and promotion of the veterinary industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clause 7 inserts a new Part VII in the National Parks Board Act to transfer to NParks, one, the relevant assets and liabilities of AVA; and two, the relevant employees of and seconded officers in AVA, with general preservation of the employment terms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Clauses 9 to 16 contain amendments to the Animals and Birds Act, Control of Plants Act, Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act, and Wild Animals and Birds Act for the purpose of transferring from the Director‑General, Agri‑Food and Veterinary Services of AVA the responsibility of administering those Acts to NParks, and to make consequential amendments to other Acts with cross-references to AVA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: There are also other amendments to the Animals and Birds Act and the Control of Plants Act to require importers of key food items to adopt plans, including preventive strategies, to mitigate the impact of supply disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These provisions are to support the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) in safeguarding our food security.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: I look forward to Members’ and Singaporeans’ support for NParks’ expanded role.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Food issues as well as wildlife management and animal welfare issues are becoming more significant these days.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is important that they be managed under specific bodies with the relevant resources and expertise.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The newly created SFA and the expanded NParks will certainly have their work cut out for them, but this reorganisation is a step in the right direction for sure.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With better defined responsibilities, they will be able to act on them more efficiently and effectively.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There is no question we must co-exist with wildlife.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But there are many cases of people feeling threatened by animals.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, there seems to be an increasing number of cases of snakes appearing in residential areas and causing alarm.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Wild boars, too, are a cause for concern, as there have been several cases of wild boars attacking people.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And let us also not forget about the monkeys harassing residents, first in the condominiums, and now in densely populated HDB estates, too.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And, recently, I received several feedback from my residents that monkeys are found at the bus stops and overhead bridge near Yishun Stadium.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They were so worried when they have children with them.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, there would be a lot on the plate for NParks to manage as I can foresee.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, a resident saw a snake in the drain in front of her unit which is on the ground floor.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And she is so worried because her grandchild was sleeping in the house.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, she called the Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES).

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: ACRES told her that the drain is a habitat for snake.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, she was told that that snake is a python, it is non-poisonous.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But can you just imagine this poor grandmother, in front of her is a snake and behind her is her grandchild?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: By the time I came to know about it, I quickly called the Town Council to send a pest controller down and catch the snake.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But by the time, it was too late.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, can you imagine how much stress it is causing to the resident living in that ground floor unit, not just her unit, but all the neighbours on the ground floor, because they do not know when the snake will appear again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I hope in cases like this, AVS and NParks can come in to help.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And following several snake sightings in the landed properties in Springleaf Estate, Springleaf Neighbourhood invited speakers from the Singapore Nature Society to give a talk, and I attended the talk as well and found that it is very informative, very useful.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I hope with more streamlined functions, NParks will now be able to do more to increase its outreach.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: NParks could work with the Ministry of Education and schools to educate students about dealing with wildlife.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Start them young so that they develop a positive interest and knowledge from a young age.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On the flip side, there are cases of humans hurting animals, too.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Although fishing is illegal along certain riverbanks, it is not uncommon to see people fishing illegally.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On weekends, especially along the Sungei Seletar in Springleaf Estate, one can see fishermen decked out in hats and fishing rods, sitting or standing on the riverbanks to fish.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is despite signages clearly stating "No Fishing" in that area.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Overfishing will result in an upset in the biodiversity of the river.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And not only that, some of the fishing rods get hooked on other river animals like otters.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: These animals will not survive from such man-inflicted injuries without the intervention of wildlife welfare groups.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My residents often gave feedback that some of these fishermen simply throw away the fishes, especially if the fishes caught are too small for them to eat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, they just throw along the riverbank and, very often, residents also found fishing hooks along the riverbank, and all these can be very dangerous when someone steps on them.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Before I conclude, I would like to reiterate that it is good to have harmonious co-existence with animals, but we need to strike a balance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We need to consider the safety of our residents first.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In Nee Soon South Zone A, many residents are complaining about sightings of big, big rats and I went down at night to take a look.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, many cat feeders mean many two hours.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: To conclude, the Government's decision to create a lead organisation for the management of animals is evident that it recognises the importance of this issue to the environment and to the hearts of Singaporeans.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is good to take care of animals.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But please do not forget to take care of our residents' safety and hygienic living environment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):  : To have peaceful co-existence with the animals is good for everybody.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Under this circumstance, you do not have to report to the Police but to look for the relevant organisation.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hopefully, the new agency can step up the education and offer help to the residents when necessary.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On the other hand, some humans may hurt animals.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will harm otters and other animals and disturb the eco-balance.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In English): Notwithstanding the above, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, in practice, most of us adopt a live-and-let-live approach.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: HDB, generally, does not take too much enforcement action as long as the keeping of cats does not affect anyone adversely and the neighbours do not complain.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, there are also cases of irresponsible cat owners who keep their cats in an unhygienic condition.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have a resident who keeps many cats in her flat and does not exercise good hygiene or proper cat litter box practice.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This case has been going on for more than four years and the stench from the cat faeces is unbearable for the neighbours.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And, every few months, the surrounding neighbours of up to 10 different households would come to see me to ask how much longer they have to suffer the stench.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are also complaints of unusual insects spotted in their flats by the neighbours, possibly attracted by the unhygienic environment.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It must be surprising that the various agencies are not able to solve this problem after four years.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, HDB does not have the power of forced entry to enter the particular flat to document the facts of the case.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The owner is uncooperative and refuses to open the door.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, HDB is unable to enter the flat to confirm the existence of the cats and to serve a summons in person on the flat owner.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am not sure if AVA has the power of forced entry.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If this is indeed the case, then another suggestion is for NParks to be given the power of forced entry to carry out its duties.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To be fair to pet owners, I believe this rule of allowing NParks to enter private property and to remove pets causing severe public disamenities should only be used when all other avenues of solving the case have been exhausted.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But nonetheless, it is a useful tool to have in cases where pet owners are uncooperative and recalcitrant.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It sets the fundamentals based on our principle of “Let's Make Singapore Our Garden” – Our Garden, referring to both flora and fauna – a vision we have set since the 1960s when we commenced our nation-building.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It also aligns with Mr Lee Kuan Yew’s vision for us in transforming Singapore into a Garden City.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With this Bill, there is a revamp of the Statutory Board and the agencies' organisations.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can I find out how this is going to affect the staffing arrangements and reporting structure?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What about the secondment of staff, with the AVA now being subsumed and transferred under NParks as well?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The transfer is appropriate, in terms of AVA coming under the same umbrella, as NParks manages our greenery and our parks, which is also the basis of our ecosystem for many animal species and types.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Coming together does make sense and helps streamline work processes and flow.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The oversight and planning of our ecosystems will also be more wholesome and aligned.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can the Minister advise us also on how the new entity will be working together with other agencies, such as the Health Promotion Board for health-related issues, infectious diseases and also health and medicinal products concerned?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How about NEA, especially pertaining to public health issues?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can we also get an update on how much, on average, do we spend on animal management annually?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I anticipate this amount is going to increase, with the new developments and changes we have planned for the next several years.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The National Biodiversity Centre has been in existence since 2006.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With this renewal of the management and plans, are there going to be changes to the focus and thrust of this Centre?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can we get an update on this as well?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With the transfer and merger effected, I assume there will be a review of our national plans.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: So, will there be any changes to our National Conservation strategy and action plans?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This will help publicise to the public information and also a single point of contact which makes it a lot easier for all forms of feedback as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, I should start by thanking her for sharing the extensive list of animals we have in Yishun and the amazing biodiversity we have.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the Senior Parliamentary Secretary will reply to some of the concerns Er Dr Lee has raised, but I would like to add that, perhaps we have so many rats also because we have removed all the pythons which eat the rats.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It addresses a significant problem we face on the ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many times, we respond to feedback related to monkeys, for example.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If that particular monkey is in a nature reserve, we would inform NParks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As we wait for NParks officers to arrive, the monkey moves, sometimes just by a few metres, and ends up outside the nature reserve.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There was once the monkey was at a bus stop, like Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has said, and we were told to inform the Land Transport Authority instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will enable a more unified and coherent approach.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I stand in support of this Bill but would like to seek a few clarifications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, I would like to seek clarifications for the rationale for limiting the definition of “animal”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The definition of “animal” under the current Act, which references the Parks and Trees Act, includes “any other living creature, vertebrate or invertebrate”.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Anthropods are now included in the definition of animals but there are invertebrates that are not anthropods.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This includes cnidarians, such as jellyfishes and annelids, such as earthworms and leeches.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify the rationale for limiting the definition of "animal" in this way?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, the positive aspect of this merger is that it will create synergy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are merging so that, instead of two organisations, we have one organisation focused on animal and plant issues.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I thus find it strange that after this merger, we then split the Director-General’s (DG's) duties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Instead of one DG, we will have four DG positions, that is, a DG for Animal Health and Welfare, a DG for Wildlife Management, a DG for Wildlife Trade Control, and a DG for Plant Health.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I understand that the DG for Animal Health and Welfare and the DG for Wildlife Management will be the same person, the DG for Wildlife Trade Control will be a different person.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I find this will complicate things on the ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, many wildlife trafficking cases involve both species protected under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) and under the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act and also species not protected by CITES that fall under the Wild Animals and Birds Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is often animal cruelty involved as well and that offence will fall under the Animals and Birds Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Prior to all the changes, this case would have been covered by one DG.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would this not be a waste of resources?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do officers handling the case have to send reports to the different DGs and the DGs will then have to meet to discuss the case?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify how the DGs will work together now, and whether there will be separate lines of reporting for enforcement officers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, I would like to focus on the issue that I have raised many times in this House, that is, culling.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Whenever we have animal-related nuisance complaints or feedback, culling seems to be the solution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Be it chickens, monkeys, birds or wild boars, we have culled them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have made progress on this front, as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary has mentioned, and now have good TNRM programmes for dogs and cats, which focus on more humane, scientific and long-term solutions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These programmes address both residents’ concerns and animal welfare concerns.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that with this merger, with NParks’ strong background in science, we will start to develop more holistic, science-based management approaches towards managing animal populations in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask that we look at this not just from an animal welfare perspective but also from an effectiveness perspective.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If culling worked, we would not have the same animal-related problems in the same areas year after year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We spend tons of resources, including financial resources, on a solution that does not seem to produce results.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a biologist by training and having done a literature review, I have found no scientific studies that support our current culling measures.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Certainly, there are no scientific studies that suggest culling based on public complaints is effective.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have to understand that with our current measures, while there is a clear reduction in numbers following a cull, at times, within a few weeks, with pigeon, for example, the pigeon numbers may be back to the pre-cull numbers and, at times, exceed it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because we usually kill the adult birds who may be the non-breeding birds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The younger, healthier and stronger breeding birds survive the cull.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: According to the Pigeon Control Advisory Service, “pigeons control their own numbers very effectively according to the volume of food available to them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: An adult pair of pigeons will usually breed four to six times a year but can breed more frequently in optimum conditions, producing two young each time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If, however, the food supply reduces and there is only sufficient food available to support the existing flock, adult birds may only breed once or twice a year or possibly not at all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Pigeons will not breed if there is insufficient food to service the needs of their young.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the food supply increases for any reason, following a cull, for example, pigeons will breed continuously until the flock reaches the point where it is fully exploiting the food available to it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In other words, there is a minor population explosion each time a cull takes place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The end result is an estimated 15%-30% increment in flock size over and above the pre-cull figure.” Sir, many others have used culling as a solution and have found as well that it does not work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the City of Basel, for example, they had 20,000 pigeons in 1963.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the culling, the population increased by 33%.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The City of Basel then focused on a public awareness campaign to address the public feeding of pigeons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It installed pigeon lofts, removed the pigeon eggs and controlled the availability of food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some culling continued during this period but that was to prevent the birds from starving to death due to the lack of food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is very different from the culling that takes place in Singapore, which takes place in response to public complaints.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The mother monkey which lost her young goes into heat again, the male monkey mates with her and another baby is born, replacing the monkey which was killed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we somehow manage to kill an entire troop, the neighbouring troop will then take over the territory of the troop who were killed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With more resources, they breed more and, sooner than later, we will have the same number of monkeys again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Culling ignores the science and puts a burden on valuable Government resources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely hope that we can move forward on this issue and that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary can share more about how NParks intends to manage the animal population in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When this merger was first announced, there were some concerns as to whether it was really true.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The problem is that it was announced that the merger would take place on 1 April, on April Fools' Day.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure there will be many benefits to be reaped from the optimisation of resources and leveraging of expertise.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think we would all agree that most of us want to live and work in environments which integrate nature with man-made structures.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Very few people would choose to live in a sterile estate with only concrete buildings.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The challenge we face is in striking a balance between the management of wildlife and human populations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Having birds and other creatures around us is good and necessary for our well-being.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, they can also be the sources of disamenity, such as noise pollution and animal waste.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some residents have shared their concerns over the population of wild birds with me, particularly species which are growing in numbers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In recent years, I have been receiving many pieces of feedback relating to problems created by increasing pet ownership in our HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some residents complain about incessant barking; others are dismayed by the foul smell of pets’ urine along common corridors and void decks; irresponsible owners who leave pets’ faeces on the ground are also a big problem.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Personally, I am quite worried about pets which are mistreated by owners who have lost interest in them, such as by confining them in small cages.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng expressed concerns about the limiting effect of the new definition of “animal” which replaces the present one in the National Parks Board Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The new definition is non-exhaustive, as signified by the use of the word “includes”.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The new definition in the Bill, therefore, allows for the inclusion of invertebrates as an animal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked why we split the duties of AVA’s DG of Agri-Food and Veterinary Services among four newly-created DGs in the Animals and Birds Act, the Wild Animals and Birds Act, the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act, and the Control of Plants Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Each Act has a significantly different and distinct purpose and scope from the other.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Hence, the Bill provides the flexibility to appoint separate technical experts for each role.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But notwithstanding this, as Mr Louis Ng has pointed out, the same person could be appointed as the DG for more than one role, if he or she has the right expertise.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Regardless of the number of officers performing these roles, they will report to the same Chief Executive Officer who will ensure that there continues to be close coordination across the different teams.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the staffing arrangements.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The senior management of AVA and NParks have engaged their staff through several townhalls and engagement sessions to ensure that they are aware of their roles and reporting structure after the reorganisation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member may wish to refer to the new section 25(6) which is inserted by clause 7 of the Bill for AVA’s non-food undertakings.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Persons on secondment in AVA’s food-related undertakings will have been transferred to SFA under the Singapore Food Agency Bill 2019 which this House has just passed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Gan Thiam Poh spoke about the need for us to co-exist harmoniously with animals, birds and other types of wildlife.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, in our biophilic City in a Garden, we live in close proximity to nature and should continue to try to minimise friction in human-animal interactions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The transfer of animal-related functions from AVA to NParks will put us in a better position to do so in several ways.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First, as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah suggested, we will continue to heighten public awareness regarding wildlife.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Should members of the public encounter wildlife, such as snakes or wild boars, they can call the existing Animal Response Centre at 1800-476-1600, which NParks will take over from AVA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is also the hotline that Prof Fatimah enquired about.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also put up advisories in parks where there have been previous sightings of wild boars so that members of the public would know how to react if they come across them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: NParks will also continue to work with nature groups, Town Councils, as well as schools on public education and engagement programmes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, AVA and NParks are members of the Long-tailed Macaque Working Group alongside volunteers from animal interest groups, such as the Jane Goodall Institute.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Working Group’s flagship community education project, the Monkey Guards Programme, teaches people how to respond to monkeys and to guide them away from residential areas.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has raised the issue about stray cat feeding.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Many community cats are taken care of by regular, responsible feeders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In this regard, agencies have worked with the Cat Welfare Society (CWS) to adopt a calibrated approach to allow such feeding whilst taking action to prevent disamenities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When NEA officers encountered cat feeders, they take down their particulars.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If the officers return and find that the site is not cleared after a reasonable amount of time, they will be able to carry out enforcement using the particulars collected earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But we take the point that Er Dr Lee has raised.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At locations where cat feeding has exacerbated rat problems, NEA and AVA will work with the CWS to tighten the processes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, feeders may be asked to clear up immediately to mitigate the problem.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Next, NParks will build on AVA’s existing partnerships with animal interest groups, animal-related businesses and other stakeholders, as it continues to refine and implement our animal and wildlife management strategy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: NParks will also work closely with other public agencies in carrying out its functions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Er Dr Lee raised the issue of illegal fishing at Sungei Seletar.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: NParks and the Public Utilities Board will continue to monitor the situation and step up enforcement where necessary.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In particular, NParks will be contributing its expertise in veterinary health and zoonotic diseases to the group.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As part of this review, NParks will engage industry players and animal interest groups to find the right balance across their various needs and interests.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A sustainable animal management strategy requires a holistic suite of measures.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This can include removal of food sources, use of contraceptives, habitat modification and population control.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Louis Ng spoke about the management of wild birds in HDB estates.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: AVA has worked closely with grassroots organisations, Town Councils and NEA to educate the public about proper food waste management, as well as stepped up enforcement in problem areas where the presence of improperly disposed of food waste exacerbates the situation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: AVA has repeatedly highlighted in its public communications that such food sources attract birds and increase their population.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This point has been carried by various media outlets, such as The Straits Times, Channel NewsAsia and Today, in their coverage of such issues.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Apart from controlling food sources, AVA has trialled various measures to move the birds away from trees near residential areas, such as the use of lasers, natural bird repellent and passing low electrical currents through roost trees.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A variety of measures are used and there is no reliance on any one single method for a quick-fix.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Taking on board the lessons that AVA has learnt in dealing with wild birds, NParks will monitor the population, occurrence, diet and movement of wild birds, so as to develop effective long-term strategies to mitigate the disamenities caused by them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, NParks is replacing roost trees with other trees that still provide shade but are less attractive to the birds, to reduce the number of roosting sites.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also found recently that with the pruning of potential roost trees, we are able to direct birds away from roosting closely to residential areas.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, by applying population studies, active tracking and modelling techniques, NParks was able to identify the various troops of macaques in the Upper Thomson area.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: NParks then worked with the grassroots leaders and residents to stem habits like feeding and poor handling of household trash, and to actively drive the macaques away from residential areas.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Only when a macaque has acted aggressively will NParks step in to relocate it, or if necessary, put it down for public safety reasons.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To address Prof Fatimah Lateef’s question about NParks’ budget for animal management, we are currently focusing on ensuring a smooth transition for all stakeholders and continuity for all existing programmes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef also asked if there would be changes to the National Biodiversity Centre, which is currently under NParks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With the reorganisation, NParks will be able to integrate its existing expertise in biodiversity, conservation and ecology with AVA’s capabilities in animal and plant health, as well as veterinary science.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will enable NParks to add new dimensions to its Nature Conservation Master Plan, which is coordinated by National Biodiversity Centre.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, NParks will be able to better incorporate the monitoring and management of zoonotic diseases into its wildlife management and species recovery programmes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Next, let me address Members’ comments on pets.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I fully agree with Mr Gan Thiam Poh that pet owners need to be responsible for the welfare of their pets.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Animals and Birds Act has mandated that pet owners show a duty of care to their pets.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: NParks will continue AVA’s good work to remind pet owners that “A Pet is for Life”.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Through the Responsible Pet Ownership programme, we hope to equip potential pet owners with knowledge on the care and responsibility that comes with owning a pet.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With the Bill, NParks will take over the administration of the Animals and Birds Act, and its officers will be suitably empowered to take enforcement action against anyone who commits an act of animal cruelty or fails to provide adequate care for their pets.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Yee Chia Hsing highlighted the issue of irresponsible pet owners in HDB flats causing disamenities to their neighbours.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In such cases, AVA, and in future, NParks and HDB will work with the flat owners, grassroots leaders and Animal Welfare Groups to resolve the issues, and to rehome the animals if necessary.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In cases where there is reasonable cause to believe that the welfare of the pets is compromised, or there is mistreatment, AVA today has powers under the Animals and Birds Act to enter the premises for investigation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: AVA can also seize the animals if there are concerns about their welfare.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To answer Mr Gan Thiam Poh, NParks officers will have these same powers even after the Bill is passed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing further suggested that agencies be given powers to forcibly remove pets from private homes due to disamenities arising from the pets but added a caveat that this should only be used when all other avenues have been exhausted.
